repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo bootstrap (TASK-0002) is the only accepted task. All 16 workspace directories exist with stub exports. Strict TypeScript, ESLint determinism rules, dependency boundary checker, and CI scaffolding are in place. No ADRs exist in docs/decisions/. CanonicalEncoder (TASK-0005) has been attempted twice and rejected both times; checkpoint-0017 records NO_ACCEPTED_CHANGES. Review-02 on TASK-0005 attempt-02 identified three MAJOR findings: cyclic containers recurse until native RangeError instead of CanonicalEncoderError, plain-object accessor hostile tests are absent, and compile/boundary validation was provided as claimed summaries rather than independently captured output.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The CanonicalEncoder has three open MAJOR findings from TASK-0005-review-02 with explicit required changes. ADR-009 must be accepted and the encoder must pass review before any StateHash implementation, which blocks the replay CLI, CI hash-comparison gate, and all FASE-1 invariant tests that depend on state hashing. The Electron installer is a locked sequencing requirement (§14.6) that has never been assigned a task and can proceed independently.

warnings: TASK-0005 has now had two rejected implementations. The cyclic-container finding (REVIEW-001) is structurally distinct from all prior rejections; the third attempt must add an active-path identity set for cycle detection using only captured intrinsics, not a general depth counter or try/catch around the native RangeError. Any cycle-detection mechanism that itself invokes user-controlled code (e.g. reading container length via an overridden property descriptor) would recreate the original category of defect.

The compile and boundary validation finding (REVIEW-003) has appeared in two consecutive reviews with different root causes each time. The next attempt must capture and attach the literal terminal output of both commands, not a human-authored summary, to satisfy the independent evidence requirement.

ADR-004 enforcement mechanism (DEFINIR) must be resolved before any bigint division is written in packages/domain. If lint-based enforcement is chosen, the rule must be active and blocking in CI before domain arithmetic is introduced, or the invariant exists in name only.
